one_liner: Salesforce B2C Commerce has broad REST APIs (SCAPI) that use OAuth-style tokens (SLAS for shopper calls, Account Manager for admin calls). They need a B2C Commerce instance and a per-merchant API client. The pages don't show a free self-serve path for an individual developer, only a shared demo sandbox and on-demand sandboxes.
auth_notes: Shopper APIs use SLAS (OAuth 2.1) with a SLAS client that is private (with a secret) or public. Admin APIs use an Account Manager token from an API client. Each merchant or realm must create its own API client. Account Manager clients can optionally authenticate with a JWT public key.
access_notes: The pages say the API is available at no extra cost to B2C Commerce customers, so access is tied to owning an instance. A shared demo sandbox and on-demand sandboxes are mentioned. The pages don't show whether an individual can get their own credentials without a customer realm. Low confidence.
blocker_notes: Needs a B2C Commerce instance (customer-owned or on-demand sandbox) and a per-customer Account Manager or SLAS API client. The pages don't settle whether a free self-serve path exists. Whether Salesforce provisions these to non-customers would need outreach.

evidence.quote: The B2C Commerce API (SCAPI) is a set of RESTful APIs for building storefronts, merchant tools, and integrations on the B2C Commerce platform.
Account administrators can use Account Manager to create API clients.
For B2C Commerce customers, the API is available at no extra cost.
If you don’t have a B2C Commerce instance, try the demo sandbox used in the example above.
To explore SCAPI with your assistant, use the [B2C MCP](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/commerce/commerce-api/guide/b2c-developer-tooling.html#connect-your-ai-assistant).
